# Psalm 34 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Of David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, so that he drove him out, and he went away.

**2** I will bless the LORD at all times; His praise shall continually be in my mouth.

**3** My soul makes its boast in the LORD; let the humble hear and be glad.

**4** Oh, magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt His name together!

**5** I sought the LORD, and He answered me and delivered me from all my fears.

**6** Those who look to Him are radiant, and their faces shall never be ashamed.

**7** This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him and saved him out of all his troubles.

**8** The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear Him, and delivers them.

**9** Oh, taste and see that the LORD is good! Blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him!

**10** Oh, fear the LORD, you His saints, for those who fear Him have no lack!

**11** The young lions suffer want and hunger; but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.

**12** Come, O children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD.

**13** What man is there who desires life and loves many days, that he may see good?

**14** Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking deceit.

**15** Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.

**16** The eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous, and His ears toward their cry.

**17** The face of the LORD is against those who do evil, to cut off the memory of them from the earth.

**18** When the righteous cry for help, the LORD hears and delivers them out of all their troubles.

**19** The LORD is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit.

**20** Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him out of them all.

**21** He keeps all his bones; not one of them is broken.

**22** Affliction will slay the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be condemned.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 34.

- **34:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **34:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **34:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **34:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **34:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **34:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **34:1**: An acrostic psalm. The superscription says 'Abimelech,' but 1 Samuel 21 calls the Philistine king 'Achish' — Abimelech may be a throne name.
- **34:21**: 'Not one of them is broken' — John 19:36 applies this to Jesus on the cross, whose bones were not broken, unlike the two criminals.

### LOGOS
- **34:9**: 'Taste and see' — experiential knowledge of God. The invitation is not to intellectual assent but to personal encounter.
- **34:19**: The psalm does not promise freedom from suffering but freedom through suffering. 'Many are the afflictions' — but deliverance from 'all.'

### PNEUMA
- **34:18**: One of the most comforting verses in Scripture. God does not merely observe the brokenhearted from afar — He draws near. Proximity is the promise.

— SOPHIA
